anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De Oratione exists (only copyrighted Greer/O'Meara/Oulton-Chadwick); nothing to compare against. Sense checked against the Greek and cited Scripture wording.

apparatus: Lk short form implies deliverance; compendious to disciple, clear to many.
Job 1:9-11; 2:4-10 long quotations; wife's rebuke; two wrestlings, third kept for Savior's three.

choices.why: stenochōreō pairs θλίβω: involuntary affliction vs voluntary yielding — the Hebrew-idiom distinction needs both verbs narrow.
Ps 4:2's ἐπλάτυνας: God widens the mind in affliction — the chapter's key term.

pass_a_gloss: Luke's short form contains deliverance in effect (compendious for the proficient, clear for the many). God delivers not by removing wrestling but in victory: afflicted-yet-unstraitened (Hebrew idiom), mind enlarged by the comforting Word. Job, authorized temptation notwithstanding, sinned in nothing and shamed the Opponent twice; the third wrestling belongs to the Savior's three Gospel temptations.
